item.title: UK confirms PM Burnham’s former fiefdom of Manchester to host G20 summit
item.description: The leaders of the world’s biggest economies will descend on Manchester next year after the UK government confirmed the English city will host the Group of 20 (G20) summit. Prime Minister Andy Burnham will use his first trip to the United Nations General Assembly in New York to announce the city he led as mayor for almost a decade as the venue for the leaders summit, according to a statement on Monday from his office. The decision to choose Manchester in the northwest of England as the centre of... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

The remarks come two days before Chinese President Xi Jinping is set to arrive in Washington to meet with US President Donald Trump for a closely watched summit where AI is expected to be on the agenda after the two... item.title: Regionales en Alemania: Merz admite derrota del CDU, AfD celebra y Die Linke avanza
item.description: Las elecciones regionales en Alemania dejaron a la CDU de Friedrich Merz en crisis, tras un revés histórico que el canciller calificó de “desastroso” al no alcanzar el umbral del 5% en algunos estados. En contraste, la ultraderecha de AfD celebró victorias inéditas: su líder Alice Weidel aseguró que el partido está listo para convertirse en una fuerza decisiva en el país. Mientras tanto, Die Linke se consolidó en Berlín, donde su candidata Elif Eralp celebró el triunfo con un mensaje de cambio social. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Top US Senate Democrat Jeanne Shaheen warns Trump not to waver on Taiwan ahead of Xi meet
item.description: The top Democrat on the US Senate’s foreign policy panel urged Donald Trump on Monday not to signal any retreat from Taiwan when he hosts Chinese President Xi Jinping this week. Speaking at the Concordia Summit in New York, Senator Jeanne Shaheen said she hoped the president “will not say anything that indicates a lack of support for Taiwan” during his talks with the Chinese leader. Shaheen is the ranking member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, which reviews US arms sales abroad,... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: UK to give support to Saudi jets in attempt to counter Houthi fighters
item.description: Andy Burnham seeks stability in Middle East to bring down prices at home as first meeting with Trump looms The UK has agreed to provide defensive air support to Saudi Arabia to help counter Houthi fighters and restore stability in the Middle East while driving down the cost of living at home, Andy Burnham has said, ahead of his first meeting with Donald Trump. The prime minister said he had agreed to a request for air-to-air refuelling of Saudi jets to defend energy infrastructure against the Iran-backed rebels and help keep oil flowing from the Gulf to ease global economic turmoil. item.description: The September 24 summit between President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump is no ordinary engagement. Their May summit took place in Beijing and largely centred on economic issues. This one will be on Trump’s home turf and is expected to put strategic questions on the table. Will the Korean peninsula and North Korea’s nuclear programme again be pushed to the margins? item.title: Alisher Usmanov, el oligarca uzbeco que hace encallar las sanciones de la UE contra Rusia
item.description: El multimillonario ruso de origen Uzbeko, Alisher Usmanov, se ha salido con la suya y ha logrado que su nombre se borre de la lista de personalidades sancionadas por la Unión Europea a causa de la invasión rusa de Ucrania. Usmanov llevaba años utilizando sus recursos ilimitados para litigar en el Tribunal de Justicia de Luxemburgo y ante los jueces alemanes, país donde solía residir, para librarse de las sanciones, pero al final lo ha conseguido cuando ha podido extorsionar al Gobierno francés a través de sus influencias en otras antiguas repúblicas soviéticas.El paquete de sanciones a Rusia… Fuente: ABC España - Internacional.

item.title: "Jefes de inteligencia europeos advierten que Moscú planea acciones contra la OTAN": 'The Guardian'
item.description: 'The Guardian' informó que el primer ministro polaco declaró ante el parlamento que las evaluaciones de inteligencia sugerían que Rusia podría lanzar un ataque con drones o misiles en los próximos meses. El presidente francés calificó de sólidas y bien documentadas dichas advertencias. La alerta también la sostuvo el servicio de inteligencia checo. Mientras que los tres países bálticos que limitan con rusia se han mostrado cada vez más cautos. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Putin ve refrendada su guerra
item.description: «Occidente ha vuelto a fracasar: los resultados de la votación confirman que la idea de infligirnos una derrota estratégica dividiéndonos desde dentro, escindiendo nuestra sociedad, está irremediablemente condenada al fracaso», escribió ayer en su canal Valentina Matviyenko, la presidenta del Consejo de la Federación, el Senado ruso. Desde la tribuna del Primer Canal, el máximo medio representante de la propaganda nacional, también se plasmaron las sensaciones del régimen sobre los comicios legislativos finalizados el pasado domingo.En ellos, el partido oficialista, Rusia Unida (RU), ganó sin… Fuente: ABC España - Internacional.

Esta investigación forma parte del Deportation Project. Romeo Langlois, periodista y reportero sénior de France 24, nos contó más sobre el desarrollo de la… Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Directo París y el aumento en los precios de la gasolina y el diésel
item.description: Este 21 de septiembre, el primer ministro francés, Sébastien Lecornu, mantiene dos reuniones para dar respuesta al aumento del precio de la gasolina y el diésel. La primera será con los directores de los centros de abastecimiento de gas y petróleo, y la segunda, con su gabinete, para tomar decisiones sobre las medidas que podrían implementarse con el fin de aliviar los costos. Informe de nuestra periodista, Natalia Ruiz. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Partido de Putin gana las elecciones legislativas en Rusia en medio de denuncias de fraude
item.description: El Gobierno ruso de Vladímir Putin recibió con buenos ojos los resultados de las elecciones, en las que el partido Rusia Unida, que ha estado en el Ejecutivo desde hace más de 25 años, logró el 57% de los votos, en medio de denuncias de fraude y después de que la mayoría de los partidos de oposición fueran excluidos del proceso. En las calles, los rusos esperan pocos cambios en la estructura del Estado, pero sí que mejore la situación económica, golpeada por la guerra con Ucrania. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Malaysia’s Negeri Sembilan royal crisis escalates as chief minister defies ruler
item.description: Malaysia’s royal crisis in Negeri Sembilan spilled into a new constitutional fight on Monday after the state’s chief minister refused to accept the ruler’s dismissal of the entire executive council – a dispute that has already brought down one government and triggered a snap election. The latest showdown comes less than a week after the executive council backed a disputed bid to remove the ruler, putting the palace and state government in conflict over both the throne and executive... Fuente: South China Morning Post.
item.dc:creator: Iman Muttaqin Yusof

item.title: Putin party retains majority in first vote since 2022 invasion of Ukraine
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin’s United Russia party won a large majority in parliamentary elections, according to preliminary results published by state media Monday, in a vote held amid Ukrainian drone strikes, cyberattacks and a crackdown on anti-war opposition. The election was the first since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. France 24 International affairs editor, Oliver Farry, shares further insights from this election. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: España ha confirmado que se prepara para uno de los peores escenarios: uno donde aviones militares y una instalación nuclear terminan mal
item.description: España ha participado en La Haya en un ejercicio internacional diseñado alrededor de un escenario especialmente complejo: varios aviones militares sufren una colisión en territorio francés y el accidente termina provocando daños en una instalación nuclear. Un escenario destinado a comprobar cómo investigarían un desastre de estas características siete países europeos. Detrás hay además una preocupación creciente: la llegada de aviones de quinta generación está haciendo que investigar un accidente militar sea mucho más complicado por la tecnología clasificada y los materiales esparcidos. Una… Fuente: Xataka.

item.title: US, China agree AI dialogue ahead of Trump-Xi summit
item.description: Chinese and US negotiators made progress on artificial intelligence (AI) and trade ahead of President Xi Jinping’s visit to the White House later this week. “We had a very successful engagement with the Chinese on trade and AI,” US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told reporters following Sunday’s eight-hour-long negotiations at JPMorgan Chase’s head office in New York. The talks had a “good atmosphere” and were “not bad”, said China’s Li Chenggang. Li’s promotion to international trade... Publicado también por: France 24 - English. Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: Will Anwar’s coalition in Malaysia implode amid Loke exit, Najib house arrest?
item.description: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim has suffered a double whammy as his Pakatan Harapan (PH) coalition scrambles to placate public outrage over disgraced ex-leader Najib Razak being granted house arrest and the shock resignation of his transport minister in protest against the royal clemency. But observers do not expect the administration, already reeling from PH defeats in two recent state elections as federal allies turned against the coalition, to implode just yet. Anwar and PH’s reformist... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: Rising toll of US-China trade, tech curbs in focus ahead of Xi-Trump summit
item.description: With President Xi Jinping expected to meet US President Donald Trump in Washington this week, attention is again turning to the tit-for-tat trade and technology restrictions between the two nations – a friction that continues to escalate despite occasional reprieves. Over the past year, tech firms and industrial manufacturers on both sides have been casualties of the ever-intensifying rivalry, even as some benefit from growing state support to cushion the blow. From lost sales and squeezed... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: Iran is suffering yet surviving under Trump’s economic warfare
item.description: As Iranians face shortages, President Donald Trump’s blockade, more so than new sanctions, is eroding the country’s economy, analysts say. But Tehran appears to remain uncowed. Fuente: The Washington Post - World.
item.dc:creator: Susannah George, Asal Abasian

item.title: German chancellor stands his ground after his party loses in state elections
item.description: German Chancellor Freidrich Merz conceded that the night spells "disaster" for the political center, but assured the public he'd push ahead with his federal agenda of tax and welfare reforms. Fuente: NPR - World.
item.dc:creator: Esme Nicholson

item.title: Russia: Kremlin party dominates controlled vote
item.description: In Russia, early results from the parliamentary election show the Kremlin-backed United Russia party leading in the tightly controlled vote. The election, the country’s first parliamentary ballot held during wartime, began on Friday and concluded on Sunday, with around 111 million people eligible to vote. Moscow’s mayor said voting went ahead as planned despite Ukrainian drone attacks. Charlotte Hughes reports. Fuente: France 24 - English.
